_note: Experimental macro pKa for nucleotides, from literature. Used for pKa READ-OFF comparison only: the ABSOLUTE net charge of a polyphosphate depends on the low-pH primary-phosphate convention (the most acidic P-OH groups of a polyphosphate have pKa below about 2, and compilations measure and assign them differently, so the number of protons counted at low pH, and with it the absolute charge, depends on the convention adopted), so we compare the engine curve's INFLECTIONS to these pKa, not the absolute Z. Values are multi-source consensus at ~25 C, I~0.1; Reference check 2026-10-05: the one DOI (10.1021/bi00903a019) resolves, and Crossref, PubMed (PMID 14069537) and the ACS page agree on title, journal, volume, issue, pages and year; the author list differs between sources (4 names at ACS/Crossref, 3 at PubMed), so it is cited as Phillips et al. The Dawson book exists (3rd ed., Clarendon Press). The Alberty value is traced to Alberty & Goldberg 1992 (DOI 10.1021/bi00158a025; I = 0.25 M) via its reproduction in Alberty's 2003 book. An earlier attribution of the low-pH convention point to Sigel could not be traced to any source and was replaced by the statement above (2026-10-05). The ATP values at I = 0.1 M are also given by Sigel et al. 1987 (DOI 10.1021/ic00260a028). No pKa value was re-checked against the full texts.
